item.title: A harmonized database of biosphere–atmosphere ammonia flux measurements across ecosystems and pollution regimes
item.description:
Tycho Jongenelen, Margreet van Zanten, Jan Willem Erisman
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08371-0
Abstract Ammonia (NH 3 ) is a trace gas with detrimental effects on human health and ecosystems. Understanding and quantification of NH 3 exchange between the biosphere and atmosphere is essential for assessing ecosystem nitrogen budgets and critical load exceedances. Yet, uncertainty in these processes remains significant, due to the global scarcity of measurements. We created a database of more than 40,000 records of NH 3 flux measurements across ecosystems, including heathlands, peatlands, grasslands, forests, croplands, and dunes, in areas with varying ambient NH 3 and sulphur dioxide concentrations, using different measurement techniques from 1991 to 2024. A significant share of measurements originates from the Netherlands, reflecting its early deployment of a high-resolution NH 3 monitoring network. Fluxes are quality controlled and harmonized using consistent algorithms, with uncertainty estimates included. Fluxes were recalculated using consistent stability correction functions, ensuring comparability across sites. By providing this database, we aim to contribute to the understanding of the NH 3 biosphere-atmosphere exchange, its environmental controls, the validation and calibration of NH 3 exchange schemes, and the characterization of NH 3 fluxes across ecosystems.

item.title: Chromosome-level assemblies of complementary haploid genomes and population resequencing for the saprotrophic bolete Buchwaldoboletus xylophilus
item.description:
Yingli Cai, Yonglin Tang, Ruzhi Luo, Zeyin He, Juyin Bai, Wenan Tu, Zhijia Gu, Xiaofei Shi, et al.
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08440-4
Abstract Buchwaldoboletus xylophilus is a rare, non-ectomycorrhizal bolete with a saprotrophic lifestyle. Here we present reference genome assemblies for two compatible haploid strains (B06 and B07) derived from a cultivated fruiting body, together with Illumina resequencing and draft assemblies for a population set of 17 isolates comprising seven monokaryons and ten dikaryons. The submitted B06 and B07 assemblies are 30.69 Mb and 30.49 Mb, respectively, each containing 13 chromosome-sized sequences, with basidiomycota_odb12 BUSCO completeness of 97.7% and 97.9% and sample-specific Merqury QV values of 51.10 and 57.17. The resource includes structural and functional annotations, repeat annotations, mating-type-locus candidates, and CAZyme predictions. Raw reads are available through NCBI SRA under study accession SRP689425; assemblies are available through NCBI GenBank and NGDC/GWH; and annotation files and supporting results are available through Figshare.

item.title: Global Multi-Index Drought (GMID): a multiscalar high-resolution dataset from 1980 to near present
item.description:
I. Noguera, B. Bulut, A. Chevuturi, L. J. Barker, J. Hannaford
Scientific Data
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-07904-x
Abstract Drought assessment is an extremely complex task that relies on high-quality datasets, posing a major challenge for scientists and water managers. Here, we present the Global Multi-Index Drought (GMID), a multiscalar high-resolution dataset that includes five standardised drought indices: the Standardised Precipitation Index (SPI), the Evaporative Drought Demand Index (EDDI), the Standardised Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI), the Standardised Evapotranspiration Deficit Index (SEDI), and the Standardised Vapor Pressure Deficit Index (SVPDI). This dataset is available globally at multiple time scales (1- to 12-, 18-, 24-, 48-month) for the period 1980–2024, with high spatial (0.1°) and temporal (weekly and monthly) resolution. The GMID dataset contains two versions of the drought indices; one generated using a traditional single-distribution approach, and another using a new flexible-distribution approach allowing the selection of probability distributions providing the best-fitting normalised series in each case. GMID adds significant value to previous drought data products through its high resolution and flexible multi-index nature, representing a comprehensive and robust long-term dataset for drought (and flash drought) assessment at the global scale.

item.title: LOCC-GER - A georeferenced local climate policy database for Germany
item.description:
Dennis Abel, Manuel Linsenmeier, Stefan Jünger, Amelie Veit
Scientific Data, vol. 13, issue 1
DOI: 10.1038/s41597-026-08183-2
Abstract Local climate action has increased massively worldwide. Germany is a noteworthy case in this respect, as local measures have been strongly promoted by the federal system over the past two decades. However, studying policies, their determinants, and consequences at this scale has been difficult so far due to a lack of centralized data. This article introduces LOCC-GER, the largest existing dataset of georeferenced local climate policy-making in Germany. The dataset currently covers 26,142 measures from 5,033 municipalities, including detailed descriptions of employed measures, funding sum, and duration from 2008 to 2023. It is extended with important local context variables on public opinion and civil society activities, as well as detailed weather and climate indicators. We demonstrate how it can be used to map and analyze local governments’ actions on climate change. Finally, we discuss how LOCC-GER may be extended by academics and other users through our proposed workflow for user-specific linking with additional covariates, offering high spatial and temporal flexibility.
